claim: RankEF ranks whole candidate code solutions by jointly learning correctness classification and execution-feedback-style explanation generation, avoiding the need to actually execute code at ranking time, and outperforms CodeRanker.
stance_target: candidate (b)/(d): using execution/requirement signal to allocate compute or guide repair
scope_conditions: three code generation benchmarks, ASE 2024, whole-solution granularity
quoted_support: RankEF employs multi-task learning to integrate code classification with execution feedback generation. This approach enables the model to understand the reasons behind incorrect code, distinguishing between correct and incorrect solutions without the need to execute the code during the ranking phase.

claim: Execution-based code ranking methods face notable limitations including scarcity of quality unit tests and security risks from running untrusted generated code.
quoted_support: Execution-based methods, although effective, encounter notable limitations, such as scarcity of quality unit tests and security risks.

claim: Code candidate ranking methods select among whole candidate programs rather than identifying and prioritizing specific failing requirements within a single program.
stance_target: novelty of per-requirement compute allocation and repair (candidates b, d)
scope_conditions: code ranking literature as of ASE 2024
quoted_support: Existing approaches typically generate multiple candidate solutions using LLMs to increase the likelihood of producing correct code. However, selecting the correct code from these candidates-a process known as code ranking-remains a major challenge.
